sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: untied date anchor selecting rate versions in a dated surcharge schedule, aggregated over a complete 13-terminal universe; medium; measured platform result remains pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 6 (D06) L152 fixes the day, 31 March 2022. Doc 2 (D02) L174-182 gives 13 import rates; on that day the four Patrick rows take their 7/03/2022 rates (135.85, 57.69, 155.40, 141.45) and the Flinders Adelaide row keeps $75.00 (its 112.50 starts 1/04/2022). Per-port sums 75.00, 497.83, 102.69, 441.90, 408.70; total 1,526.12; mean 1,526.12 / 13 = 117.3938 -> $117.39. Inputs: one date, 13 rates, two effective dates.
- Universe: Attachment A lists exactly 13 stevedore-port rows (Adelaide 1: Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal; Brisbane 4: AAT, DP World Australia, Hutchison Ports, Patrick; Fremantle 2: DP World Australia, Patrick; Melbourne 3: DP World Australia, Patrick, VICT; Sydney 3: DP World Australia, Hutchison Ports, Patrick). D10 L19 names the same five ports as the ACCC-monitored international container ports; D08 L283 ("all three container stevedores", Melbourne) and D13 L167 ("3 stevedores", Port Botany) agree with the Melbourne and Sydney rows. D02 L87 (ACCC quote) says Patrick has 4 terminals, matching its four rows. No other document lists a container terminal at these ports with a surcharge.
- Necessity: D06 is the only source of the exemption's last day ("31 March" occurs only at D06 L152; D19 L205 says the exemption followed the January 2022 flood but gives no end; D17 L24 calls it "temporary legislation", undated; D09 L57 and D13 L102 date only the floods). Without D06 the day could fall before 7 March 2022 ($111.55), between 7 and 31 March ($117.39) or from 1 April ($120.28), so the answer cannot be fixed; a model that recalls the end date could bypass D06 (stated risk). D02 is the only per-terminal source: D08 L131/L206 ("more than $140.00 per TEU", "up to $140.00 per container"), D19 L336 ($80.00 in February 2019), D13 L222 (2,600%), D03 L96 ($122 and $152 per container, no terminal) and D11 L49-54 (chart without values) give no terminal rate for 2022. The wording names ports and the count but no rate or date, so both documents stay indispensable.
- Selected-lever checks: Scatter the pieces: the day is only in D06, the rates only in D02. Same series, right edition: the "edition" is the rate version in force on the day; using the 25 January 2022 versions gives $111.55, using every scheduled version gives $120.28. Calculate across documents: the mean is printed nowhere. Not claimed: exact table vs rounded prose, which-items, exclusion.
- Targeted failure modes: Failure mode 1 $111.55 (1,450.13 / 13), Failure mode 2 $120.28 (1,563.62 / 13), Failure mode 3 $114.43 (1,487.63 / 13), all recomputed (scratchpad calc_i01.py and the per-port cross-check). No platform attempts yet. Considered and not declared: the export column (on that day 1,260.77 / 13 = $96.98), ruled out by the question's "import"; D02 Table 1 averages ($121.87 NSW, $118.59 QLD, $128.51 VIC, "$122,99" eastern seaboard), ruled out by its 2017/2021 columns and three-state scope; adding GST (no rate is given anywhere in the bundle).
- Calculation verification: author scripts (Python Decimal, 2026-10-08): day-by-day rate selection over the 13 rows (calc_i01.py) and an independent per-port subtotal route (Adelaide 75.00, Brisbane 497.83, Fremantle 102.69, Melbourne 441.90, Sydney 408.70); both give 1,526.12 and 117.393846 -> $117.39. The reasoning sums the 13 printed rates in one step so every operand is a Doc 2 figure. No knife-edge: 0.0038 above 117.39 and 0.0062 below the 117.395 rounding boundary. Date convention: "until 31 March 2022" read inclusively (last day 31 March); an exclusive reading (30 March) gives the same rates; Patrick's increase dated 1 March (text) or 7 March (table) gives the same rates.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: grep for "31 March", "March 2022", "April 2022", "exemption", "infrastructure surcharge", "per full container" and "average" across D01-D20: the day is only in D06 L152; per-terminal rates only in D02 L174-182; printed averages only in D02 Table 1 (2017/2021, three states). No document prints 117.39, 1,526.12 or a 2022 national mean. The task page overview lists "31 March 2022" among Doc 6's dates and "1 March 2022 · 7 March 2022" among Doc 2's, with no surcharge figures. Shortest complete route: D06 date, then all 13 D02 rows with their effective dates, then one mean.
- Precision/readings: answer in dollars to the cent as asked; all 13 rates are printed to the cent and exclude GST alike; the mean is unweighted across terminals (no volumes are given). The table lists no rate change after 25 January 2022 other than Patrick's and Flinders Adelaide's, so every other row is taken at its printed rate on 31 March 2022. D08's "up to $140.00 per container" (VTA, Melbourne, approximate, no terminal) is not a terminal rate and does not change any input.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json: incomplete false, gap 0 for all 20 documents).
- Style/set review: plain wording, no em dashes. Rev 2 is 27 words (rev 1 was 47), below the 28-47 band named by the form's length-spread advisory (Feedback log, index F1). Kept from rev 1: "coastal-trading" (a bare "WA exemption" could be read as Fremantle Ports' Cargo Berth Hire exemption for vehicles, D07 L119-121, which ended in September 2021), "last day" (not "ended", which could mean 1 April, when Adelaide's new rate starts), "import", "infrastructure", the count 13 and the five ports. Dropped: "temporary", "container and roll-on, roll-off voyages" (D06's own phrase), "stevedore", "per full container" and "container" before "terminals"; the 13 import infrastructure surcharges exist only in D02 Attachment A, which is per full container, and the automotive terminals in D07 carry no such surcharge, so the universe and basis are unchanged. sections.question: On the WA coastal-trading exemption's last day, what mean import infrastructure surcharge did the 13 terminals at Adelaide, Brisbane, Fremantle, Melbourne and Sydney charge, to two decimals?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source fact (Doc 6, section on a permanent coastal trading exemption): the Federal government's section 11 exemption of the Coastal Trading (Revitalising Australian Shipping) Act 2012 for voyages by container and roll-on, roll-off vessels to Western Australia applied until 31 March 2022, so its last day was 31 March 2022.

Step 2. Source fact (Doc 2, Attachment A title, header and narrative): the national stevedore infrastructure surcharges are listed per full container, excluding GST, as at 25 January 2022, in columns for stevedore, port, export, import and effective date. Doc 2's text says the latest increases by Patrick Terminals are shown on the right-hand side and will be implemented on 1 March 2022.

Step 3. Source fact (Doc 2, Attachment A rows with no later rate): the import surcharge per full container was $100.00 at AAT Brisbane (effective 1-Jul-21), $128.90 at DP World Australia Brisbane (1-Jan-22), $133.08 at Hutchison Ports Brisbane (1-Mar-21), $45.00 at DP World Australia Fremantle (1-Jan-21), $144.70 at DP World Australia Melbourne (1-Jan-22), $141.80 at VICT Melbourne (1-Jan-22), $131.60 at DP World Australia Sydney (1-Jan-22) and $135.65 at Hutchison Ports Sydney (1-Mar-21). None of these rows lists a later rate.

Step 4. Source fact (Doc 2, Attachment A Patrick rows): Patrick's import surcharge from 1-Mar-21 was $113.20 at Brisbane, $53.85 at Fremantle, $129.50 at Melbourne and $117.85 at Sydney. Each Patrick row adds a right-hand import rate dated 7/03/2022: 135.85 at Brisbane, 57.69 at Fremantle, 155.40 at Melbourne and 141.45 at Sydney.

Step 5. Source fact (Doc 2, Attachment A Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal row): the import surcharge was $75.00 from 1-Jul-21, with a right-hand import rate of 112.50 dated 1/04/2022.

Step 6. Date check (from Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5; Doc 6 and Doc 2): Doc 2 writes these dates day first, since its text puts Patrick's increases in March (1 March 2022) while the table dates them 7/03/2022. Patrick's increases had taken effect by 31 March 2022, so that day its import rates were 135.85, 57.69, 155.40 and 141.45. The Flinders Adelaide increase starts on 1/04/2022, the day after 31 March 2022, so that terminal still charged $75.00.

Step 7. Count (from Steps 3 to 5; Doc 2): the table lists 1 terminal at Adelaide, 4 at Brisbane, 2 at Fremantle, 3 at Melbourne and 3 at Sydney: 1 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 13 terminals.

Step 8. Calculation (from Steps 3, 5 and 6; Doc 2): sum of the import rates in force that day, in the table's order (Adelaide; Brisbane AAT, DP World, Hutchison, Patrick; Fremantle DP World, Patrick; Melbourne DP World, Patrick, VICT; Sydney DP World, Hutchison, Patrick): 75.00 + 100.00 + 128.90 + 133.08 + 135.85 + 45.00 + 57.69 + 144.70 + 155.40 + 141.80 + 131.60 + 135.65 + 141.45 = $1,526.12.

Step 9. Calculation (from Steps 7 and 8; Doc 2 and Doc 6): mean import surcharge = 1,526.12 / 13 = $117.39 (to two decimal places).
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Superseded date or version
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date
Where the trap sits: Doc 2, Attachment A, titled "INFRASTRUCTURE SURCHARGES - AS AT 25 January 2022 per full container / excluding GST". Its labelled columns (STEVEDORE, PORT, EXPORT, IMPORT, EFFECTIVE) give the rates in force when the table was compiled. On Patrick's four rows the labelled import rates, $113.20 at Brisbane, $53.85 at Fremantle, $129.50 at Melbourne and $117.85 at Sydney (effective 1-Mar-21), are followed by unlabelled right-hand rates dated 7/03/2022: 135.85, 57.69, 155.40 and 141.45. Doc 2's text says these increases "will be implemented on 1 March 2022".
The wrong answer a careless solver gives: $111.55. A solver who reads only the labelled IMPORT column treats the 25 January 2022 snapshot as the rates on the question's day. The 13 labelled import rates sum to 1,450.13, and 1,450.13 / 13 = 111.55, so the answer looks like a clean average of the printed table.
Why the correct answer avoids it: The question fixes the day by the exemption's end, and only Doc 6 dates it: the exemption for container and roll-on, roll-off voyages to Western Australia ran "until 31 March 2022". That is after Patrick's increases took effect (7 March 2022 in the table, 1 March in the text), so on that day Patrick charged its right-hand rates. Swapping them in adds 22.65 + 3.84 + 25.90 + 23.60 = 75.99 to the sum, giving 1,526.12 and a mean of $117.39.

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Out-of-range period
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date
Where the trap sits: Doc 2, Attachment A, Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal row: "Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal Adelaide $75.00 $75.00 1-Jul-21 79.50 112.50 1/04/2022". Like the four Patrick rows, it carries an unlabelled right-hand pair of higher rates, but these start on 1 April 2022, one day after the exemption's last day in Doc 6. Doc 2's narrative mentions only Patrick's increases and says nothing about the Adelaide change, so a reader who has just learned to use the right-hand Patrick rates can easily treat this pair as one more rate already in force.
The wrong answer a careless solver gives: $120.28. A solver who sees that the question's day falls after the table's 25 January 2022 date, and therefore swaps in every right-hand rate without checking each one's own start date, also replaces the Adelaide rate with 112.50. That adds 37.50 to the correct sum, giving 1,563.62, and 1,563.62 / 13 = 120.28.
Why the correct answer avoids it: A careful reader checks each right-hand rate's own date against the exemption's last day, 31 March 2022, instead of assuming that every listed increase has already started. Patrick's rates dated 7/03/2022 apply on that day; the Adelaide rates dated 1/04/2022 only begin the following day. On 31 March 2022 the Adelaide terminal therefore still charged $75.00, so the sum stays at 1,526.12 and the mean is $117.39.

### Failure mode 3
Trap: Document convention
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date
Where the trap sits: Doc 2, Attachment A writes its two scheduled dates as bare numbers, "7/03/2022" on the four Patrick rows and "1/04/2022" on the Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal row, while the labelled EFFECTIVE column spells the months out ("1-Mar-21", "1-Jan-22"). The table itself never says whether the day or the month comes first in those numeric dates, so a reader used to month-first dates can misplace both changes by several months.
The wrong answer a careless solver gives: $114.43. A solver who reads the numeric dates month first takes Patrick's increases as starting on 3 July 2022, which is after 31 March, and the Adelaide increase as starting on 4 January 2022, which is before it. That keeps Patrick's four old rates but applies the Adelaide rate of 112.50, so the sum is 1,450.13 + 37.50 = 1,487.63, and 1,487.63 / 13 = 114.43.
Why the correct answer avoids it: Doc 2's own narrative says Patrick's increases "will be implemented on 1 March 2022", which fits 7/03/2022 only if the day comes first, so the table follows the day-first convention throughout. Reading both dates that way puts Patrick's change on 7 March and the Adelaide change on 1 April. On 31 March 2022 Patrick's new rates and the Adelaide terminal's old $75.00 therefore apply, and the mean is $117.39.
